title: Variational Routing: A Scalable Bayesian Framework for Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Transformers
claim: Deterministic routing is brittle under input noise, while mild stochasticity in routing improves both calibration and accuracy over the baseline.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, left-to-right, dual y-axes with shaded variance bands in (b)
description: Two line plots side by side, captioned (a) Brittleness of Deterministic Routing and (b) Calibration-Accuracy Trade-off. Panel (a) plots expert consistency (Jaccard similarity) against noise level sigma from 0.001 to 0.05. A bold red line with shaded ±1σ layer-variance band falls from about 0.98 to 0.15, well below a dashed grey line marking ideal stability at 1.0. Panel (b) uses dual y-axes against temperature T from 0.1 to 2.0. A blue line shows calibration error (ECE, lower is better) and an orange dashed line shows accuracy (higher is better), each with a translucent band. Dotted horizontal baselines mark the reference ECE and accuracy. Both metrics improve at low temperature, and the lines cross near T=1. The eye goes first to the steep red decline in (a), then to the blue and orange curves in (b).
caption: Motivation. (a) Deterministic routing is empirically brittle to input noise. (b) Simple low-temperature sampling ($T{<}1$) creates a "sweet spot" that improves both Calibration (Blue $\downarrow$) and Accuracy (Orange $\uparrow$) over the baseline (dotted). Both motivational experiments' details can be found in Appendix [ref].
abstract: Foundation models are increasingly being deployed in contexts where understanding the uncertainty of their outputs is critical to ensuring responsible deployment. While Bayesian methods offer a principled approach to uncertainty quantification, their computational overhead renders their use impractical for training or inference at foundation model scale. State-of-the-art models achieve parameter counts in the trillions through carefully engineered sparsity including Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers. In this work, we demonstrate calibrated uncertainty at scale by introducing Variational Mixture-of-Experts Routing (VMoER), a structured Bayesian approach for modelling uncertainty in MoE layers. VMoER confines Bayesian inference to the expert-selection stage which is typically done by a deterministic routing network. We instantiate VMoER using two inference strategies: amortised variational inference over routing logits and inferring a temperature parameter for stochastic expert selection. Across fine-tuning tested foundation models, VMoER improves routing stability under noise by 38\%, reduces calibration error by 94\%, and increases out-of-distribution AUROC by 12\%, while incurring less than 1\% additional FLOPs. These results suggest VMoER offers a scalable path toward robust and uncertainty-aware foundation models.
